chapter_title: Chương 17: 0017【Làm cách nào để kiếm tiền?】

segments.title: Chương 17: 0017【Làm cách nào để kiếm tiền?】
segments.content:
What kind of business could one do in a small, eighteenth-tier city like Longdu in the early 2000s?

It seemed there were none.

There were already a few large and medium-sized supermarkets in the city center, though one could open a small community supermarket. But Chen Guiliang had no capital.

Although the county town didn't have any Western fast-food chains, the city proper already had a KFC.

Start a Chinese fast-food restaurant?

Heh, that wouldn't succeed even in twenty years.

This was one of the birthplaces of the three major schools of Sichuan cuisine. The palates of the diners were extremely discerning. Anyone who tried to open a Chinese fast-food joint was doomed to fail.

Dealing in things like video discs and cassette tapes might have been profitable over a decade ago, but now the market was completely saturated.

He had to focus on the internet.

Taobao was actually the first choice, but it wasn't suitable here. The problem of express delivery couldn't be solved.

Of course, he could arrange for direct shipping from the manufacturers. The problem was, once sales took off, the partner manufacturer would inevitably cut him out. In an emerging market, the brand of your online store was worthless. You had to stock your own inventory to guard against the manufacturers.

The direct-shipping model would only be useful after competition on Taobao became fierce.

"Talk business?"

Feng Tao shook his head repeatedly as he listened. "I'm just a poor working stiff, and you're just a poor student. What business do we have to talk about?"

Chen Guiliang asked, "How many shares do you have in this shop?"

"Only 20%. The other 80% belongs to my high school classmate," Feng Tao sighed. "I'm still deep in debt just to buy into it."

This cousin-uncle was the son of Chen Guiliang's grandaunt (his paternal grandmother's biological sister).

He happened to be ten years older than Chen Guiliang.

Feng Tao was also a child from the countryside who graduated from a junior college in the mid-1990s.

Back then, a junior college degree still held decent value.

But Feng Tao had floundered in Yangcheng and Pengcheng for several years without much success. He had also been hurt by love, and in his despair, he chose to return to his hometown, accept his parents' arranged blind dates, and get married.

It wasn't until the beginning of this year that an old high school classmate got him into running private servers for Legend of Mir. After making a little money, they switched to selling computers.

After finishing the call with his wife, Feng Tao said to his assistant, "You can get off work now."

The assistant, a bit dull-witted, smiled, bowed, and said goodbye.

After the assistant left, Feng Tao introduced him, "That's my apprentice, Yang Xiaolong, from the neighboring Yangjiaba Village. He didn't continue his studies after failing the college entrance exam this year. Now he's learning how to build and repair computers with me. He's still not very good with people, but he's a fast learner."

"Cousin-Uncle, are you still running private servers for Legend of Mir?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Before his rebirth, although Chen Guiliang had worked in the gaming industry for many years, he had always been in operations and marketing.

He knew nothing about technology.

Now, if he wanted to make a fortune in gaming with little capital, his only option was to try his hand at private Legend of Mir servers.

But the development of private servers went through several stages, so Chen Guiliang first had to inquire about the current situation.

"I just stopped," Feng Tao said.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Why did you stop?"

Feng Tao explained simply, "More and more people are setting up private servers, and the competition is too fierce. It's no problem to make a little money, but it's very difficult to make big money. It's better to just sell computers honestly."

In the autumn of 2003, private Legend of Mir servers were experiencing their first boom period.

Private servers with various versions were sprouting like mushrooms after a spring rain. There were too many competitors, the market was severely homogenized, and there was a lack of innovation. It was no longer a time when you could easily pick up money.

Moreover, in just over a month, five ministries would launch a joint special rectification campaign, which would scare many forums and private server operators into disappearing for good.

Feng Tao continued, "My classmate can't even be bothered to promote online anymore. He only sets up private servers in his own few internet cafes. They're all barely scraping by, just enough to make a little extra cash."

Chen Guiliang asked again, "With your skills, Cousin-Uncle, can you design a private server yourself?"

Feng Tao shook his head. "I'm self-taught in programming, a total amateur. My skills are just so-so. I can only buy other people's server frameworks and make minor modifications here and there. I could probably design one if I had to, but it would be the simplest kind. Adding a few more features would cause bugs."

Chen Guiliang was a bit disappointed. The first partner he had envisioned was, of course, his trustworthy cousin-uncle.

It seemed he had to find someone else now.

Chen Guiliang asked again, "How much does it cost to buy a private server framework?"

"You want to run a private server when you don't know anything about it?"

Feng Tao teased him, but still answered seriously, "Anywhere from a few hundred to tens of thousands of yuan. The more expensive ones are of course better."

A server framework for a few hundred yuan would definitely be a run-of-the-mill product with no appeal.

One for tens of thousands, however, would have various unique features and could be customized according to one's own ideas.

Chen Guiliang had no capital right now, only the living expenses his parents gave him. He certainly couldn't afford a server for several thousand or tens of thousands of yuan.

He planned to incorporate pay-to-win elements, but he didn't know the technology himself. He needed to bring in a financial backer and find some technicians to modify and maintain the game.

Sigh, if only I had learned programming in my past life.

Not knowing technology was quite awkward now.

Chen Guiliang changed the subject. "Cousin-Uncle, can you tell me about your high school classmate?"

Feng Tao said, "His name is Tao Chenggang. Both his parents were workers at the boiler factory, a state-owned enterprise. Like me, he only got into a junior college. But he's quick-witted. He somehow made a few hundred thousand yuan and returned to Longdu a couple of years ago to open internet cafes."

"Now he has eight internet cafes, a game studio for gold farming, and an 80% stake in this computer shop. He was also the one who got me into running private Legend of Mir servers to make money."

Chen Guiliang said, "I'd like to pay him a visit."

"What do you want to see him for?" Feng Tao treated Chen Guiliang like a little kid.

Chen Guiliang said, "Just arrange a meeting."

Feng Tao thought it over and felt it wouldn't cause any harm, so he nodded. "Okay, I'll help you set it up. But tomorrow and the day after are holidays, and I can't leave the shop. You'll have to go find him yourself."

"Thank you, Cousin-Uncle." Chen Guiliang offered another cigarette.

"Why are you being so formal with me?"

Feng Tao tucked the cigarette behind his ear, got up, and prepared to close the shop and go home.

Chen Guiliang followed his cousin-uncle to the parking area and soon saw his ride—a second-hand Jialing motorcycle.

"You're a boss, after all. You drive this piece of junk?" Chen Guiliang teased.

Feng Tao complained bitterly, "Boss, my ass. The money I earned working in the south was all spent when I got married. Then I partnered to open this shop this year, and my share of the private server money wasn't nearly enough. Add the mortgage for our marital home, and I'm over sixty thousand yuan in debt."

Chen Guiliang offered some auspicious words, "Selling computers is very profitable. A few tens of thousands is nothing, you'll make it back in a year or so."

"I hope so," Feng Tao said, straddling the motorcycle.

The residential complex where his cousin-uncle lived was quite high-end. They had bought it two years ago when it was the most expensive real estate in the city, at about 1,000 yuan per square meter.

The price had gone up now, to 1,100 per square meter.

Feng Tao opened the door and went inside. The sound of stir-frying came from the kitchen.

His cousin-aunt, Lin Chunhong, called out from inside, "You two go ahead and sit down. There's one more dish!"

Feng Tao turned on the TV and plopped down on the living room sofa.

Chen Guiliang walked to the kitchen doorway. "Cousin-Aunt, sorry to intrude. I came in such a hurry I didn't even buy any fruit."

Lin Chunhong said, "It's fine, you're family. No need to buy fruit."

Looking at the small child on his cousin-aunt's back, Chen Guiliang felt extremely complicated.

Lin Chunhong was very beautiful, the village belle type.

But she wasn't very worldly and hadn't even finished high school. When she married his cousin-uncle, she wasn't even of legal age. They held the wedding banquet a good half-year before officially registering their marriage.

For now, she was quite a virtuous wife.

In a few years, when the family became well-off, her heart would grow wild.

She would meet someone online and cheat on his cousin-uncle.

Let's just say she went to learn a new skill. For the sake of their child, the couple divorced and then remarried.

Later, his cousin-uncle was diagnosed with stomach cancer. Half of his stomach was removed, and he once recovered. Not two years later, it relapsed. His cousin-aunt, Lin Chunhong, insisted on a divorce and, despite his illness, made a scene demanding to sell the house and car to divide the assets.

His cousin-uncle passed away from the illness.

His cousin-aunt vanished without a trace, completely abandoning her son.

The son lived with his grandparents, but they too passed away one after another. In the end, it was Chen Guiliang's parents who stepped in to adopt him.

In other words, the little child on Lin Chunhong's back at this moment was, in the legal sense, Chen Guiliang's younger brother.

The boy was quite sensible and later went to military school.

"Cousin-Aunt, let me hold the baby for you. It's not convenient for you to cook like this," Chen Guiliang said, walking into the kitchen.

Lin Chunhong immediately put down her spatula, untied the baby from her back, and handed him to Chen Guiliang.

"Waaah, waaah..."

The moment Chen Guiliang took him, his little cousin-brother started wailing.

Feng Tao laughed from the living room. "Hurry and bring him to me. You can't handle him."

Chen Guiliang quickly passed the little cousin-brother over, and the house finally quieted down.

Feng Tao played with his son, saying proudly, "This kid is shy with strangers. He won't let anyone hold him except his mom and dad."

Chen Guiliang played along, "It's good for boys to be a bit rowdy."

Feng Tao boasted, "When we have money in the future, we'll pay the fine and have a daughter. I don't have any great ambitions in life, just to have both a son and a daughter."

They were simple, ordinary words, but hearing them from his cousin-uncle's mouth, Chen Guiliang felt a surge of emotion.

Chen Guiliang said, "If you want both a son and a daughter, you need to take good care of your health. You could get a full-body check-up every year."

Feng Tao joked, "I'm in great health. I'm not going to donate money to the hospital."

Chen Guiliang knew that persuasion was useless. He could only wait a few years and then use the excuse of getting a check-up himself to drag his cousin-uncle to the hospital with him every year when he came back to his hometown.

The two of them, uncle and nephew, watched TV, teasing the child and chatting idly.

Before long, Lin Chunhong brought the dishes to the table and served them rice as well.

Feng Tao showed off, "Your cousin-aunt has no other virtues, but you won't find another as good a wife as her. Tao Chenggang... that's my high school classmate, he's green with envy every time he comes over for dinner, saying I must have stepped in dog poop to have landed such a good wife."

"Aunt is indeed very virtuous," Chen Guiliang nodded in agreement.

Lin Chunhong smiled and went to take her son. "Give him to me, it's time for him to nurse."

Feng Tao brought out a bottle of Wuliangye. "How about a couple of drinks with me? This is good stuff. Tao Chenggang gave it to me. I usually can't bear to drink it."

Chen Guiliang reached out and placed his hand on the bottle. "Cousin-Uncle, drinking is bad for the stomach. I hear frequent drinking can easily lead to stomach cancer."

"Stomach cancer my ass. Let me pour you a glass," Feng Tao said hospitably.

Chen Guiliang could only remain silent.

Feng Tao had a good tolerance for alcohol, which he had developed from his time as a salesman in Yangcheng.

He had to go to the shop tomorrow, so he only drank until he was slightly tipsy.

After dinner, Feng Tao, a little buzzed, made a phone call:

"Hey, Brother Gang... It's me... I have a nephew who's heard of you and wants to pay you a visit... He's not in business, still a student..."

"Hey now, the kid is a top student, in the experimental class at No. 2 Middle School, he can easily get into a 985 university... Just meet him for a moment, it's not like it'll cost you millions... Okay, okay, it's settled then."

Tossing the phone onto the sofa, Feng Tao rubbed his face and said to Chen Guiliang, "Tomorrow morning, I'll give you a ride to the game studio. You can wait for him there. You might have to wait for an hour or two, but he has to go there in the morning anyway."

"Okay, sorry to trouble you, Cousin-Uncle," Chen Guiliang said.

Feng Tao reminded him, "This guy is loyal and loves making friends, and he's extremely concerned about face. As long as you give him enough face, everything will be fine. Let me put it this way, when he was in high school, he had the exact same temper as you. He once even took a knife and injured someone to avenge a friend. He's much smoother now, hasn't been in a fight for years."

Chen Guiliang felt like he was looking in a mirror and laughed. "People like that are actually easy to deal with. You just have to find the right way to stroke their ego."

"That's exactly it," Feng Tao agreed.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What does his game studio do?"

Feng Tao chuckled at the thought. "You'll know when you get there. He even gave the game studio a nickname: 'Longdu City Internet Addiction Treatment Center'."

"Sounds like an interesting guy," Chen Guiliang couldn't help but smile.

Feng Tao said, "Don't be so quick to disbelieve it. The studio's only been open for a little over a year, and it's already cured more than ten students of their internet addiction. Some parents have even gone there specifically to present him with silk banners."

Silk banners, for crying out loud!

Chen Guiliang said, "Cousin-Uncle, can I use your landline?"

"Go ahead," Feng Tao said, dozing off on the sofa.

Chen Guiliang took out a piece of paper with a number on it and dialed the pager service using the landline. "Hello, please forward to xxxxxx... Leave the message: 'Son, at Cousin-Uncle's house'."

His father didn't have a mobile phone and still used a pager.

About ten minutes later, his father, Chen Xinghua, called back. "Are you out of living expenses again? I'll send you money tomorrow."

"Not for now, you can send it next month," Chen Guiliang asked, "Dad, how much debt does our family have left?"

Chen Xinghua was silent for a few seconds. "These past two years, your mom and I switched to doing renovations, and we're earning more than when we were on construction sites. Don't worry about these things, just focus on your studies. Don't worry about university tuition either, I'm already saving up."

"How much debt is left?" Chen Guiliang asked again.

Chen Xinghua said, "It's almost all paid off, just under twenty thousand left."

A mere twenty thousand yuan in debt was not a small sum that a migrant worker in 2003 could easily come up with.

Moreover, Chen Guiliang was about to go to university, so his parents had to work to pay off the debt while saving for his tuition and living expenses.

"Is Mom next to you?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Chen Xinghua said, "Your mom was just taking a shower. I came out to make the call by myself."

Chen Guiliang said, "Then you two should get some rest."

"Okay, I'm hanging up," Chen Xinghua said. "Long-distance calls are expensive, and I didn't want to go find a public phone stall this late at night."

A phone stall was a small shop specifically for making calls, where long-distance calls were only 30 cents a minute.

Using a public phone in a regular shop was much more expensive for long-distance calls. It was 80 cents per minute for calls within 800 kilometers, and it went up to 1 yuan for distances over 800 kilometers.

To save on the phone bill, Chen Xinghua didn't talk much and hung up right on time.

Chen Guiliang also hung up the phone and went to lie down on the sofa.

He hoped that tomorrow's business meeting would be successful so that his parents could be freed from their hardships soon. They hadn't dared to return home for seven years.

After thinking for a moment, Chen Guiliang went back to the landline and dialed Bian Guanyue's mobile number.

Bian Guanyue had never given him her number.

But he had memorized it today, when his cousin-uncle was writing the receipt.

Chen Guiliang had always had a good memory since he was a child.
